svg.text: Arduino Uno scans the panel; the Pi 5 runs Monolith. Pi 5 + DAC8x / ADC8x + jacks: rear console. Hinged frame: 10.1 in screen only.
Add a 100 nF capacitor across VDD-VSS right at the chip.
Piezo, resistor and zener all sit in parallel. Solder them together at the piezo,
then run two wires (signal + GND) to the multiplexer board.

g.text: 24 keys on three 74HC165 shift registers (only 3 Arduino pins: D2 latch, D3 clock, D4 data)
D2 -> SH/LD pin 1 of all three chips
D3 -> CLK pin 2 of all three chips
Chain: chip 3 SER (pin 10) -> GND; chip 3 QH (pin 9) -> chip 2 SER; chip 2 QH -> chip 1 SER; chip 1 QH -> D4.
Every chip: VCC pin 16 -> 5V, GND pin 8 -> GND, CLK INH pin 15 -> GND, 100 nF across VCC/GND.
Each of the 24 keys: one MX switch between its input and GND,
plus a 10k pull-up from that input to 5V (use 3 x 9-pin 10k
bussed resistor networks, common pin to 5V). 30 MX switches
total: 24 here + 4 arrows, OK and SONG (Pi).

svg.text: Rear lights: WS2812 strip data -> D5 via 330 ohm, 5V + GND, 470 uF across the strip.
26 pixels: 0-11 VU left, 12-23 VU right, 24 PLAY, 25 REC. Plain green power LED: 5V-330R-LED-GND.
5. Top panel layout (to scale, along the 7 deg slope)
hinged display frame pivots on the rod behind the panel
grey dots = lid screws M3 x 10, red = split straps (under the lid). Full-size copy: panel_artwork.svg
5a. Rear console, front face (to scale): logo, lights, VU meter, between the two hinge ears
VU windows 7 x 4 mm at 10 mm pitch (WS2812 strip behind, diffuser tape); LEDs 5 mm.
5b. Side view: wedge body, wooden cheek and hinge rod (to scale)
rear console: rod, Pi 5 + HAT, jacks
panel slopes 7 deg; 4 wood screws per side through the wall; full-size template: cheek_template.svg
jacks, ports, Pi + HAT: in the rear console
frame 270 x 172 x 30 mm, ears on the M8 rod
nuts give friction; closed (-90) to +45 deg
only 2 thin cables cross the hinge:
6. D-pad, OK, jog wheel and SONG key to the Raspberry Pi GPIO (BCM numbers)
Other side of every switch + encoder common
GPIO 2-4 and 18-27 are kept free for the DAC8x + ADC8x. Keep SPI off (9, 10, 11).
No resistors: the Pi's internal pull-ups are used. Switches and the encoder connect the pin to GND.
The Pi sits in the rear console: a 10-wire ribbon (9 signals + ground) from the body through the back-wall slot to the header.
POWER: 12 mm momentary button on the back -> the Pi 5's 2-pin J2 'power button' header. Press = start / clean shut-down; hold = force off.
PHONES: small stereo headphone amp board on the floor behind the front-right corner, input from OUT 1/2 (parallel with the jacks),
its 9 mm level pot through the front wall (LEVEL), 1/4 inch stereo jack next to it (PHONES). Power it from the 5 V rail.
BACK, as you face it, left to right: POWER, 5V IN (USB-C), LAN, USB | IN L, IN R; below: OUT 1 ... OUT 8; vents behind the Pi.
All names are engraved into the wall. Audio: 5 short 3.5 mm stereo leads, cut, each soldered to two mono 1/4 inch jacks:
DAC8x jack 1/2 -> OUT 1 + OUT 2, 3/4 -> OUT 3 + 4, 5/6 -> OUT 5 + 6, 7/8 -> OUT 7 + 8; ADC8x input 1/2 -> IN L + IN R.
In each lead: tip -> tip of the odd jack (OUT 1, 3, 5, 7 / IN L), ring -> tip of the even jack, sleeve -> both sleeves. No other ground wires.
